**Finding: missing (high severity) — Termination for convenience (T4C)**

The agreement runs three years (§ 8.1) but Section 9 provides only cause-based exits (material breach, insolvency, security/service-level/legal/IP failures), and the numbering jumps from 9.3 straight to 9.5 — there is no convenience right at all. Worse, § 2.1 locks Customer into a USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights."

Redline (validated, preferred position):
- **New § 9.4** — Customer may terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, on 30 days' written notice, with refund of prepaid Fees for the post-termination period and no early-termination fee; Vendor expressly has no convenience right during a term.
- **§ 2.1** — conformed so the take-or-pay commitment reduces pro rata for, and does not override, Customer terminations under Section 9.

Note on direction: Vendor has no convenience right anywhere in the document, so nothing needed deleting on that side. Fallback available in negotiation is 60 days' notice.
